paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. Jacob is scared of what's coming, and he ends up alone in the dark, wrestling a man until daybreak. When the man says, "Let me go, for it is daybreak," Jacob replies, "I will not let you go unless you bless me." He holds on and asks for the blessing (Genesis 32:26).

And look at what he walks away with. The man tells him, "Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with men, and you have prevailed" (Genesis 32:28). Then he blesses Jacob there (Genesis 32:29). Jacob says, "Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared" (Genesis 32:30). I think the lesson is that bringing your fear straight to God and not letting go is no small thing.

Now, he leaves limping (Genesis 32:31). I think he got the blessing and the limp in the same night, and the limp is part of what he carries out of there. So when your own night gets long, baker, bring it to God and hold on tight. I'll be over here trying to hold on to a hot cookie sheet for more than two seconds.
